title: Standby fails to decode WAL when the primary is stopped
body: I'm running PostgreSQL 15.2 on Ubuntu 22.04. When I stop a primary server, its standby can fail during WAL replay with `invalid memory alloc request size 2021163525`, after the WAL stream connection closes. The stack shows `XLogDecodeNextRecord()` passing an `xl_tot_len` read from WAL to `XLogReadRecordAlloc()`. At `NextRecPtr` 0/B1703FF0, the standby's WAL contains repeated `0x78` bytes where the primary has a record header. I supplied a TAP test that reproduces the failure by repeatedly restarting a primary with a standby; running copies of it in parallel on tmpfs eventually makes `pg_ctl stop` fail because the standby startup process exits.

symptoms_visible: When I stop the primary, the standby can log `invalid memory alloc request size 2021163525`, terminate its startup process, and shut down.
At the failing next-record position, my standby WAL contains repeated `x` bytes while the primary WAL contains a record header.
My parallel TAP reproducer eventually fails because the standby startup process exits and `pg_ctl stop` fails.
N0.label: N0 standby WAL replay failure reported

symptoms_visible: On Debian 9, the new recovery test initially exits before running subtests because its header-scanning Perl code is unsupported there.
With `wal_log_hints = on`, the new end-of-WAL test also fails even though the rest of check-world passes.
N1.label: N1 portability and test-stability problems reported

symptoms_visible: The revised test works on Debian 9, but with `wal_log_hints` the branch patches pass on REL_12_STABLE and REL_13_STABLE and still fail on some other branches.
N2.label: N2 revised test still unstable across branches

symptoms_visible: I retested the final candidate patches for all branches, with `wal_log_hints`, under Valgrind, and with my original standby restart reproducer, and found no issues.
N3.label: N3 final candidate comprehensively verified

symptoms_visible: The maintainer reports that the WAL-reader fix and its follow-up correction have been pushed; I verified the final candidate patches before landing, but I have not retested a post-landing build on my standby.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix pushed without post-landing reporter retest

question_patterns: Could you run the latest patch set and its recovery test on your older Debian environment and paste any failure?
Please test the current version with check-world on Debian 9 and report the raw TAP output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On Debian 9, `t/039_end_of_wal.pl` returned 25 with no subtests. The log says `could not find match in header access/xlog_internal.h`. The `@{^CAPTURE}` construction is not supported by Perl 5.24; replacing it with an older-compatible capture made the test work.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The test passes unchanged on Debian 9 with its bundled Perl.
The core standby process still exits with the same invalid allocation while running the latest patched build.

question_patterns: Can you also run the recovery test with your non-default test configuration and report whether its result changes?
Does the current test remain stable when you enable your usual extra configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With `TEMP_CONFIG=extra.config` and `wal_log_hints = on`, this new test fails even though check-world passes without it. Other settings may affect it too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The test is stable under every extra configuration I tried, but the original standby restart reproducer still crashes.

edges.comment: Reporter participant1, c50: Alexander tested the proposed recovery tests on Debian 9 and with wal_log_hints. These are raw test-harness observations from the original reporter's systems, not conclusions about the WAL-reader mechanism.

question_patterns: Could you retest the revised patch set on the supported branch versions and list which configurations pass or fail?
Please rerun the updated tests on Debian 9 and across the branch patches, including your extra configuration.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The revised version now works on Debian 9. With `wal_log_hints`, the v7 patches pass on REL_12_STABLE and REL_13_STABLE but still fail on other branches. I also noticed minor commit-message and review-line discrepancies.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same branches pass, with only a wording discrepancy in one commit message.
Every branch still fails the new test at the original invalid memory allocation.

edges.comment: Reporter participant1, c55: Alexander retested v7. The branch-specific wal_log_hints results prompted further correction of the test's WAL-position and previous-record-link accounting.

question_patterns: Please retest the latest candidate comprehensively and report the results before it is committed.
Can you run the current branch patches with your extra configuration, Valgrind, and the original reproducer?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I've retested this version for all branches, with `wal_log_hints`, with Valgrind, and with my `099_restart_with_stanby.pl` reproducer. I found no issues; in my opinion it is ready.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My original restart reproducer still causes the standby startup process to exit with an invalid allocation on the candidate patch.
All functional tests pass, but Valgrind makes the same suite substantially slower.

edges.comment: Reporter participant1, c58: final pre-landing verification by the original reporter. This is a measurement edge; the answer records only the test matrix and observed result.

solution.intent: Fix WAL decoding so a record header split across pages is fully read and validated before trusting its total length for an oversized allocation, while retaining the minimum record-length guard before CRC validation and covering malformed end-of-WAL cases with controlled recovery tests.
solution.concrete_example: Reorder the WAL-reader path so it may reuse an existing decode buffer without allocating, then read the next page and validate the complete split header and continuation-page metadata before permitting a larger allocation. Keep the short-record rejection before CRC calculation, and add controlled tests for malformed record and page-header fields. The main change was pushed, followed by a correction restoring the short-length guard and adding an assertion after slow build-farm systems exposed that omission.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the failing stack, differing WAL bytes, reproducer, and pre-landing test results. Engineers concluded that a split record header allowed recycled or unwritten standby WAL bytes to be treated as xl_tot_len before complete cross-page validation. They also determined that the first simple validation patch could silently stop replay of a valid oversized record, and that the initially landed rewrite had accidentally removed a short-record check needed before CRC validation.

edges.comment: Main resolution from participant2 c61 and corrective follow-up c79-c83. The original reporter verified the final candidate in c58, but did not report a retest of the landed code. Build-farm operators exposed the missing minimum-length check after the initial push; that maintainer-side evidence informs the final technical solution without being presented as the reporter's own test output.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: while a WAL record header spans a page boundary, the reader can treat recycled or unwritten standby WAL bytes as xl_tot_len and attempt a huge allocation before completing the normal cross-page header validation.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the supplied stack, the standby-versus-primary WAL bytes at NextRecPtr, and the reproducer or controlled recovery tests.
The fix must validate the complete split record header and continuation-page metadata before allowing an oversized allocation, while retaining the minimum record-length check before CRC validation.
Must not recommend only an early maximum-length cap that treats the record as end-of-WAL; the thread found that approach could silently terminate replay of a valid oversized record.

Must acknowledge that the reporter verified the final candidate patch but did not retest a post-landing build, and must ask for verification on a build containing the fix before declaring the reporter's system resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical PostgreSQL user and test contributor; comfortable with gdb, WAL hexdumps, TAP tests, parallel stress runs, Valgrind, stable-branch builds, and old Perl environments.
persona_hint.communication_style: Precise, evidence-heavy, and cooperative; supplies raw logs and reproducible tests, retests multiple revisions, and reports portability or test-stability problems without overstating conclusions.
